newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO WALKS OUT ON DUTCH "COFFEE SHOPS".
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO WALKS OUT ON DUTCH "COFFEE SHOPS".

text.p: The largest bank in the Netherlands, ABN AMRO NV, said on Thursday it would stop doing business with coffee shops, the infamous Dutch establishments that sell small amounts of soft drugs.
ABN AMRO spokesman Theo van Dijk said the bank's position in dealing with these businesses was becoming more uncertain as the Dutch government tightened its liberal soft drugs policy.
He said the bank had been writing to clients who run coffee shops, advising them it would end their relationship.
"We don't want to be associated with illegal activities," he told Reuters.
Soft drugs such as cannabis and marijuana are technically illegal in the Netherlands but the use of small amounts is tolerated, particularly in the estimated 1,200 coffee shops in the country.
The Dutch defend the policy of decriminalising soft drugs on the basis that it keeps young people away from "underworld" pushers of hard drugs and does not increase soft drug use.
But Dutch authorities have been tightening regulations governing coffee shops in recent months following publicity linking these drugs with serious crime.
